newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee easier, pre-harvest supply tight.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee easier, pre-harvest supply tight.

text.p: Indonesian Robusta coffee prices were generally easier on Monday in line with falls in London last Friday as supply and stocks remained thin ahead of the harvest start next month, traders said.

They said the local price was quoted at 3,150-3,200 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, down from 3,450-3,550 rupiah a week ago. The export price was quoted at $1,350-$1,400 per tonne FOB Lampung against $1,500.
The traders also said they expected London coffee to open $20-$30 down later on Monday, but it was expected to rebound on news of a drastic drop in Colombia's 1996/97 coffee output.

John Naranjo, commercial manager of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said last Friday the country's 1996/97 production could drop to as low as 10.4 million 60-kg bags, from 12.9 million bags in 1995/96.
"The drastic drop in the crop more than justifies the fears about tight supplies," he told a meeting in Armenia, Colombia.
"I see London prices opening $20-$30 down, before picking on the Colombian news," one Indonesian trader said. "The news has been well digested by the market, and could lift prices."
The trader said Indonesian coffee supply was tight, with not much stocks in the hands of exporters.
"Local prices are relatively high, while buyers are offering relatively low prices," he said. "It's a big headache because local prices are too high, while buyers are offering too low."
"Under such conditions, it is difficult to do business."
Another trader said supply was expected to be tight until the harvest begins in earnest late next month, adding that some were selling the new crop forward, but in small quantities.
"There is some short covering going on by exporters looking to fill contracts, but volumes have generally been small," he said. "The lack of beans is posing a big problem."
